business.what_it_does: Loops is an email sending platform for SaaS teams to send marketing, product, transactional, and lifecycle email from one place.
business.business_model: Contact-based subscription: paid plans are priced by subscribed contacts, with no seat fees or per-send charges.

facts.statement: Loops combines marketing, product, transactional, and lifecycle email in one platform.

provenance.quote: Loops is the email sending platform for SaaS teams. Send marketing, product, and transactional lifecycle email from one place, from waitlist to IPO.

facts.statement: Loops supports marketing and transactional email, integrations, APIs, webhooks, deliverability guidance, SDKs, a CLI, agent skills, and an MCP server.

facts.statement: Product-email workflows can be built around product events for onboarding, trials, and re-engagement.

provenance.quote: Build onboarding, trial, and re-engagement workflows around your product events. Keep contact data current so each email reflects the user’s latest state.

facts.statement: Loops offers official SDKs for Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, Nuxt, PHP, and Ruby.

facts.statement: Integrations can sync contacts, trigger workflows, and send transactional email; custom setups can use incoming webhooks or the Loops API.

If you’re looking for the fastest way to get started, try Zapier or Make. For custom setups, use incoming webhooks or the Loops API.

- sending Supabase Auth emails
- syncing Supabase users into your Loops audience.

facts.statement: Paid pricing is based on subscribed contacts; unsubscribed contacts do not count, and every plan permits uploading unlimited contacts.

facts.statement: Loops does not charge separately for team seats.

provenance.quote: No, Loops does not charge for team seats. You can invite your team without adding a separate per-seat fee to your plan.

facts.statement: Loops says every plan includes workflows, events, and contact properties.

provenance.quote: Every Loops plan includes workflows, events, and contact properties.

facts.statement: Loops provides DNS records for sending-domain setup and applies DKIM signing from the first send.

provenance.quote: Loops provides the records you need. You copy them into your DNS during domain setup, and DKIM signing is active from your first send.

facts.statement: Framer reportedly sends all of its newsletters, product campaigns, onboarding flows, and transactional email through Loops.

provenance.quote: Framer sends 100% of its email through Loops, from newsletters and product campaigns to onboarding flows and transactional email.

facts.statement: Trails reportedly set up Loops in 30 minutes and averages a 40% open rate on product updates.

provenance.quote: Ryo set up Loops in 30 minutes. Now an agent builds the emails, and their product updates average a 40% open rate.

objections.objection: We already have separate providers for marketing and transactional email; consolidating them will create migration risk without a clear enough payoff.
objections.answer: Loops supports marketing, product, and transactional email from the same contact record. Cosmos is documented as replacing SendGrid and Braze with Loops for onboarding, transactional email, and monthly product updates, while Framer is documented as sending all of those email types through Loops. These examples establish feasibility, but the supplied evidence does not quantify migration effort for a typical buyer.

objections.objection: Connecting our product data, events, and authentication system will take more engineering time than this is worth.
objections.answer: Loops offers official Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, Nuxt, PHP, and Ruby tooling, plus APIs, webhooks, integrations, a CLI, agent skills, and an MCP server. Supabase and Clerk have documented paths, but the evidence does not promise a universal setup time or remove the engineering required for custom event schemas and lifecycle logic.

objections.objection: The Supabase Send Email Hook setup is too elaborate; I only want auth email working quickly.
objections.answer: Loops documents SMTP as the quicker route for confirm-signup, magic-link, invite, change-email, and reset-password messages. Both SMTP and the hook use the same Loops transactional emails, so a team can start with SMTP and move to the hook later without rebuilding templates. SMTP still requires structured Loops payloads and does not cover every hook action type.

objections.objection: At $49 per month, this is premature for our current audience and email volume.
objections.answer: The Free plan is $0, does not expire, permits unlimited uploaded contacts, and includes up to 4,000 combined marketing and transactional sends to the first 1,000 contacts in a rolling 30-day window. It includes Loops branding and the stated send limits, so this only resolves the objection for teams that fit within those constraints.

objections.objection: Contact-based pricing could become expensive as our audience grows, even if our sending volume is modest.
objections.answer: Paid pricing counts subscribed contacts rather than total uploaded contacts; unsubscribed contacts do not count, and paid plans do not add per-send or transactional-send charges. The evidence does not show that this model is cheaper for a buyer with many subscribed contacts and low send frequency.

objections.objection: Unlimited sends sounds risky or misleading if throughput and deliverability controls are weak.
objections.answer: Paid plans allow up to 1,000 emails per second per team and enqueue excess email. Loops documents DKIM signing from the first send after domain setup, automatic suppression of hard bounces and spam complaints, send pacing, and retries. Authentication is explicitly described as necessary but not sufficient, so the evidence does not guarantee inbox placement.

objections.objection: A single platform for every email creates too much vendor concentration and makes a future move harder.
objections.answer: Loops demonstrates that one platform can cover marketing, product, lifecycle, and transactional email, and it provides APIs, webhooks, SDKs, SMTP, and contact uploads. However, the supplied evidence does not establish data-export completeness, template portability, workflow export, or a low-cost exit path, so this objection is not fully answered.

objections.objection: We need proof that Loops can handle meaningful scale before trusting it with critical account and transactional email.
objections.answer: Runable reportedly sent more than 10 million marketing, lifecycle, and transactional emails through Loops in about a year, and Framer reportedly sends 100% of its newsletters, campaigns, onboarding flows, and transactional email through Loops. These are vendor-published customer stories, not independent reliability benchmarks or uptime guarantees.

objections.objection: Our preferred language or framework is not officially supported, and relying on an unreviewed community SDK is unacceptable.
objections.answer: Loops officially supports Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, Nuxt, PHP, and Ruby, while custom implementations can use its API, incoming webhooks, or SMTP. Community SDKs are explicitly described as unreviewed and unendorsed, so buyers outside the official set may still need to build and maintain their own integration.
